description: Deliver a NEW forced-rebuild strategy for the stuck PostgREST schema cache (PGRST205 on jobs/job_applications/banners), since grants + full rebuild + plain NOTIFY + one project restart all failed. Create supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql which forces PostgREST to fully rebuild its schema cache by emitting real DDL events on the exposed public schema (COMMENT ON SCHEMA + create/drop a disposable throwaway table) combined with NOTIFY pgrst 'reload schema' and 'reload config'. The Flutter data-access stays byte-for-byte identical to the working campaigns .from() path (no code changes). Also deliver supabase/PGRST205_RUNBOOK.md, a concise Hinglish runbook for a stressed non-technical user documenting the run order and the Dashboard fallbacks (Exposed-schemas toggle, then project Restart). This feature is self-contained and has no dependencies.
steps: Create supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql. It MUST be idempotent (safe to run repeatedly) and contain, in this order: (1) a header comment explaining this is the forced-rebuild method for a stuck PostgREST cache and that free-tier API cache can lag several minutes; (2) `COMMENT ON SCHEMA public IS 'reload schema';` (a DDL event PostgREST's event trigger listens for); (3) a DO $$ ... $$ block that runs `CREATE TABLE public._pgrst_cache_bust (x int);` then `DROP TABLE public._pgrst_cache_bust;` so the create+drop emit ddl_command_end / sql_drop events that force PostgREST to notice schema changes - use a clearly disposable throwaway name (_pgrst_cache_bust) and DROP it in the same block/script; guard with IF EXISTS on a pre-drop so re-runs are clean; (4) `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';` then (5) `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload config';` as the final two statements so the file ENDS with the reload NOTIFYs.

Inside FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql, embed as SQL comments (-- ...) the exact Dashboard runbook: OPTION B Exposed-schemas toggle = Settings -> API -> Exposed schemas -> remove `public` -> Save -> wait 30s -> re-add `public` -> Save -> wait 60s; OPTION C = Settings -> General -> Restart project, done AFTER the schema toggle. Include a note that free-tier PostgREST API cache can take several minutes to refresh.

Do NOT include any DROP TABLE / DROP of the real jobs, job_applications, or banners tables anywhere in the file. Do NOT create any new user-facing table. The only table touched is the disposable public._pgrst_cache_bust which is created and dropped within the script.

Create supabase/PGRST205_RUNBOOK.md: a concise Hinglish (Hindi in Latin script) runbook for a stressed non-technical user. Document the exact step order: (1) run supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql in the Supabase SQL Editor -> wait ~1-2 min -> hit Retry on the Jobs/Banners screen; (2) if still PGRST205, do the Exposed-schemas toggle (remove public, Save, wait 30s, re-add public, Save, wait 60s) -> Retry; (3) if still failing, Settings -> General -> Restart project -> wait ~5 min -> Retry. State clearly what success looks like (Jobs and Banners screens load real data, no DBG3/PGRST205 error). Keep it short and reassuring.

Do NOT modify any .dart file, and do NOT modify lib/**/error_utils.dart. Confirm the .from() calls in lib/features/jobs/providers/jobs_provider.dart and lib/features/home/providers/banners_provider.dart remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql exists and contains `COMMENT ON SCHEMA public IS 'reload schema';`, a DO block that creates and drops public._pgrst_cache_bust, and ends with `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';` followed by `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload config';` as the last executable statements.

supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql contains NO DROP of the real jobs/job_applications/banners tables and creates no new user-facing table (only the disposable _pgrst_cache_bust, which is dropped in the same script).
supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql embeds, as SQL comments, the Exposed-schemas toggle steps and the Restart-project fallback, plus a free-tier lag note.
supabase/PGRST205_RUNBOOK.md exists, is written in Hinglish, and lists the ordered steps (run SQL -> wait -> Retry -> toggle -> wait -> Retry -> Restart -> wait -> Retry) and describes success.
No .dart files are modified (git status shows only the two new files under supabase/ plus task-state files).
verification: Run `grep -n "COMMENT ON SCHEMA public IS 'reload schema'" supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql` and confirm one match.
Run `grep -n "_pgrst_cache_bust" supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql` and confirm both a CREATE TABLE and a DROP TABLE for it exist.
Run `tail -n 5 supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql` and confirm the last two executable statements are NOTIFY pgrst 'reload schema' and NOTIFY pgrst 'reload config'.
Run `grep -niE "DROP TABLE (IF EXISTS )?(public\.)?(jobs|job_applications|banners)\b" supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql` and confirm ZERO matches.
Check balance of parentheses, single quotes, and $$ dollar-quote delimiters in FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql (even count of $$).
Confirm supabase/PGRST205_RUNBOOK.md exists and run `git status --porcelain` to confirm no .dart files are modified.
findings: Delivered two files: supabase/FORCE_SCHEMA_RELOAD.sql and supabase/PGRST205_RUNBOOK.md. No .dart files touched (git status --porcelain shows only the two new supabase files plus task-state). SQL uses a NEW method vs prior failed attempts: instead of relying on plain NOTIFY, it emits REAL DDL events on the exposed public schema (COMMENT ON SCHEMA public IS 'reload schema' + a DO block that DROP IF EXISTS / CREATE / DROP a disposable throwaway table public._pgrst_cache_bust) so PostgREST's ddl_command_end/sql_drop event triggers force a full cache rebuild, then ends with NOTIFY pgrst 'reload schema' and NOTIFY pgrst 'reload config' as the final two statements. Idempotent and safe to re-run; does NOT drop/recreate the real jobs/job_applications/banners tables and creates no user-facing table. Dashboard fallbacks (Exposed-schemas toggle, then project Restart) are embedded as SQL comments plus a free-tier lag note. Static verification (network INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, Flutter/Dart not installed, live DB unreachable, so no execution possible): COMMENT ON SCHEMA appears exactly once; both CREATE TABLE and DROP TABLE for _pgrst_cache_bust present; last two executable statements are the two NOTIFYs in order; grep for forbidden real-table drops returns 0; executable SQL is balanced (parens 1/1, single quotes 6, $$ count 2, all even). Full-file paren/quote counts look uneven only because of comment prose; executable-only lines are fully balanced. Runbook is written in Hinglish with ordered steps (run SQL -> wait ~1-2 min -> Retry -> Exposed-schemas toggle -> Retry -> Restart -> Retry) and a clear success description. Did NOT commit/push/branch per orchestrator instructions.
